source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Hardware Status" -> "Sensors"
Compare each sensor's reading and setting with BMC sensor spec.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor Reading & Threshold is human reable and match with spec.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor get 'TEMP_CPU0~1' 2>&1; echo ---SDR-FALLBACK---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr elist 2>&1 | head -100
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: returns FULL raw `ipmitool (OOB lanplus) sensor get "<SENSOR>"` reading + threshold; user judges (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES sends `CPU0~1` as one quoted sensor name even though the title notation may denote two records. It does not inventory populated sockets, bind CPU numbering to physical packages, prove both sensors exist, collect untruncated thresholds/status or compare WebUI/spec fields; its credential/cipher assumptions are unapproved.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires per-CPU topology and evidence. V3.1 further makes acceptance population-aware, requires an explicit CPU0/CPU1-to-socket/APIC/FRU map, keeps per-socket results separate and rejects a combined/average value or one populated sensor as proof of both.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 872/2291 accepts the literal range string and output presence without resolving whether it names one record or two, verifying CPU population/socket mapping, capturing both UI rows or checking specification thresholds/freshness.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1035 draft exists in the invalidated 1,000-record run.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the `0~1` notation; ED-34 treats topology/population/spec/Script as readiness; ED-35 keeps the source read-only and does not add stress; ED-38 requires credential-safe complete evidence, no clear/write/retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify every CPU temperature sensor represented by `TEMP_CPU0~1`—normally CPU0 and CPU1 for populated sockets—is individually readable in Hardware Status > Sensors and has the correct socket identity, value, units, health state and applicable thresholds for the platform specification.
original_method: Discover actual CPU/socket population and separate stable sensor records rather than querying the tilde expression literally, map each record to its physical package and WebUI row, then compare complete read-only fields with the per-socket sensor specification under the recorded host load. Logs and thresholds remain unchanged.
manual_activity: The platform owner defines CPU numbering and expected sensors for the fitted socket population and supplies per-socket specifications. Automation can collect each record and WebUI row independently; a human resolves socket-label or absent-socket ambiguity and owns the verdict. No load or thermal stimulus is authorized by this row.
required_inputs: Exact chassis/board/BMC/BIOS/CPU topology with populated sockets, CPU model/stepping and mapping among physical socket, OS/APIC package and BMC CPU index
Stable sensor ID/name/number/type/entity/instance and Hardware Status row for each expected CPU
Per-CPU expected Celsius scaling/rounding, tolerance, threshold capability/values/hysteresis and health/unavailable semantics
Recorded host power/load/frequency state, BMC and optional host package-telemetry source, timestamp alignment and allowed update lag/delta
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, supported transport/cipher and protected authentication
Pinned immutable accessible `sensor.git` revision/checksum with safety review, or approved manual collection method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL or system logs; they provide thermal/throttling context and are unrelated to this read-only display check.

Do not issue `sensor get 'TEMP_CPU0~1'` unless the vendor proves it is a literal record. Enumerate the actual CPU0 and CPU1 records and never treat one response, wildcard-like notation or an average as both sockets.

Do not assume index equals physical socket. Bind each sensor using SDR entity/instance plus platform topology and record absent sockets as not populated only when the approved configuration confirms that state.
Do not add CPU stress, change power/fan policy or alter thresholds to make readings differ. This case verifies present values/settings; dynamic thermal response belongs to another approved test.
Do not require thresholds the SDR capability mask marks unsupported, but do not accept missing required per-CPU limits. Preserve units, scaling, status and freshness for each socket separately.

Do not truncate fallback data, expose passwords with `-P`, assume cipher 17 or execute the unavailable Script before review. Stop without automatic retry on swapped/duplicate sensors, stale data or UI/OOB disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, CPU population/topology, client and Script; enumerate complete sensor inventory and establish an expected CPU-sensor matrix before selecting any record.
Capture each expected CPU sensor's full raw/API identity, reading, units, thresholds, capability/status and timestamp plus its separate unchanged WebUI row.

Compare per-socket fields with Project SPEC and optional time-aligned host telemetry using approved scaling/lag/tolerance, reporting missing, swapped, duplicate, absent-socket and stale cases independently.
Confirm no state mutation, preserve raw/redacted evidence and never clear logs, create load, alter settings, retry automatically or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the fitted CPU population and cross-layer CPU0/CPU1-to-socket mapping plus expected sensor matrix.
Provide per-socket thresholds/status/tolerance/freshness and optional host-telemetry equivalence, and approve the Script/tool.
Review each socket independently and issue the formal verdict without allowing one CPU's evidence to substitute for another.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Likely unfit literally because `~` is title range notation rather than an SDR wildcard, and one output cannot prove two socket records. It also omits topology, UI/spec correlation and complete fallback, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate the complete sensor repository, resolve separate vendor-defined CPU0 and CPU1 sensor names/IDs for populated sockets, retrieve each through protected access and compare each unchanged WebUI row and full threshold/status set independently with the platform matrix.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_CPU0~1, Hardware Status > Sensors, reading/setting comparison, readability/spec Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; the Review layer interprets range notation without editing the Master and adds no stress.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a population-aware two-row evidence matrix keyed by physical CPU socket and stable SDR identity, then compare raw/API and WebUI values per socket with versioned specifications at a recorded passive load state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact board/CPU population/BMC/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record CPU model/stepping, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform CPU topology and sensor map, CPU/BMC thermal limits, SDR definition, WebUI schema and Project configuration specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves tilde notation into explicit population-bound records, validates every socket separately and protects evidence/access without introducing active thermal stimulation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static per-CPU readings do not validate stress response, throttling, thermal control or alarm transitions; one socket cannot cover another and an absent unpopulated socket is not automatically a failure.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Population/topology map, per-socket sensor/spec matrix, load/time/tolerance rules, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BMC numbering can differ from OS/socket labels; readings may lag or use different die/package sensors; UI may omit absent sockets or round values.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or host telemetry as an approved alternate/corroboration only with preserved original ipmitool method, actual interface/version, reason, engineer approval and per-socket field equivalence. A combined CPU metric or evidence from one socket cannot be declared equivalent to both CPU0 and CPU1 coverage.
expected_evidence: Target board/BIOS/BMC, fitted CPU models and physical socket-to-BMC/OS/package numbering matrix
Complete expected sensor inventory and separate CPU0/CPU1 raw records with stable IDs, readings, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamps
Separate redacted Hardware Status > Sensors evidence for each expected populated socket with exact field mapping
Per-socket Project specification plus recorded load/power state, optional host reference, scaling/tolerance/update-lag calculation and comparison
Explicit absent-socket, missing, duplicate or swapped-sensor disposition and pinned Script/tool security evidence
No-clear/no-write/no-stress/no-retry proof, final BMC/host health, limitations and engineer-owned per-socket verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The tilde notation is ambiguous as a command operand but reasonably denotes a range of CPU sensors; Items, Procedure and Criteria still align on read-only per-sensor specification validation. Exact population/mapping is a Project readiness input rather than a core contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: CPU temperature display/spec comparison is clear. The socket population, sensor names, mapping and expected values can be supplied, so the case is PACKAGE rather than permanently BLOCKED; literal execution waits for those inputs.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE and replaces a likely invalid literal range query with complete per-socket discovery, mapping and UI/spec evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid read-only classification while strengthening population-aware acceptance, per-socket non-substitution and immutable Script governance.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists reasoning with explicit two-socket identity and field-level evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed literal tilde lookup, a combined reading or CPU0-only evidence from being presented as two-socket coverage and prevents legitimate unpopulated-socket absence from being misclassified.
independent_technical_reasoning: `CPU0~1` is human range notation, not a guaranteed IPMI sensor identifier. Multi-socket platforms can number packages differently across BMC, BIOS and OS, so the evidence must be joined through topology rather than index assumption. Each populated socket has independent sensor/threshold/status acceptance, while passive readback cannot establish active thermal behavior.
